Sent on, with your background as you wrote it and your email. The team is offline this evening and picks it up tomorrow at 10am ET, and any reply comes to your email, so you don't need to wait here.

Good mix of experience for this gear, for what it's worth. Anything else I can help with while you're here?
Copy this is exactly what i was looking for, thanks for the assist.

Happy to help. One thing I'm curious about, since you've run NiceHash rentals and tuned power settings: what pulled you toward a support role rather than staying on the BD side?

Either way, you're welcome in our Discord if you're not already there, https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, plenty of miner talk and JD is active in it.

I enjoy helping people more then i do with partnerships and deals. Networking is nice sometimes but keeping repeat customers are just as important as creating new ones as they serve as your referral network indirectly.

That's the right instinct for this inbox, most of our day is repeat buyers on pre-orders.

One more, if you don't mind: do you run any miners at home yourself right now, and if so what?

Currently running GPU mining, i plan to have some fun with some lottery miners -- and doing research on what asics (higher wattage) i can run with my current power draw since my electricity is free. Need to make sure im not overdrawing on a circuits.
Read the bsb b30 page
Read the magic miner 40t page
Searched the catalog · Harlo B30 Magic Miner 40T lottery miner

Free power changes everything, so watts matter only for your breakers.

Rule of thumb on a US 120V circuit: 15A gives you about 1440W continuous, 20A about 1920W. The Magic Miner 40T pulls ~650W at 40 TH/s ($799), the Harlo B30 ~485W at 30 TH/s ($899). So two 40Ts fill a 15A circuit and that's it, GPUs included.

Both are solo-cap····, which is the lottery-miner fun you're after. What's your panel situation, spare 20A circuits or just wall outlets?
Just wall outlets so i have to be mindful of how much load im putting on my walls.

Then eco modes are your friend, and so is spreading the units across outlets on different circuits (outlets in different rooms usually are).

The B30 drops to 230W at 18 TH/s in ECO, the 40T to 450W at 30 TH/s. At those numbers you can run a couple without touching your GPU rig's headroom. A cheap plug-in watt meter is worth the $20, it tells you what each outlet is really carrying.

Both are pre-orders, so I'd check their ship dates before you commit. Want me to?
Im good for now thanks. Ill keep this in mind for future.

Sounds good. Your note is with the team either way, and they'll come back to you by email.

If you want to keep an eye on the gear in the meantime, our Discord is the best place for it: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf. Good luck with the lottery miners.
Copy that. Take care.
You too. Good luck with the application.
